reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identified the adult-carrier genomes and convergent AMR–virulence observations as additions to the dataset. The final paper documents the multi-cohort genomic study and AMR/virulence findings in P:S-e3800ae797789c38fcce and P:S-18ca49eb939b3521f0de.

A reviewer characterized the genome analysis as offering limited findings beyond surveillance. The final paper presents a surveillance-oriented collection and its stated first-setting contribution in P:S-e3800ae797789c38fcce and P:S-845f4bf435e81b78ff61.

The reviewer described a detailed genomic overview spanning prevalence, population structure, virulence, AMR, and plasmids. P:S-e3800ae797789c38fcce and P:S-23d2c496c364b247c2f4 substantiate those final-paper elements.

The reviewer specifically noted that healthy-adult carrier genomes add insight and include convergent AMR–virulence features. The final paper reports carrier and bloodstream isolates with genomic AMR/virulence characterization in P:S-d424640e86bd00886c1e and P:S-18ca49eb939b3521f0de.

Reviewers questioned comparability of cohorts sampled at different times and locations and the scope of country-level inference. The final paper retains a 2010–2020 single-hospital bloodstream collection and a distinct farmer cohort in P:S-613f60a5753b85f6bd26 and P:S-24af2d239a0c639c8295, so the sampling-scope limitation remains.

The reviewer requested a clearer distinction between genotype-defined hvKp isolates and clinically defined hypervirulent infection. The final paper states that no consensus definition exists and uses molecular virulence markers, while reporting iucA-PCR classification in P:S-b051b07d265d018725df and P:S-e3800ae797789c38fcce; this supports a residual interpretation caveat.

The reviewer asked that infection-versus-carriage prevalence emphasis be tempered because collection windows and sample sizes differ. P:S-e3800ae797789c38fcce and P:S-24af2d239a0c639c8295 document the distinct cohorts underpinning the remaining scope question.

The reviewer requested a reminder that the collection is defined by characteristic genomic features rather than by demonstrated hypervirulent disease. P:S-b051b07d265d018725df and P:S-e3800ae797789c38fcce provide the final-paper basis for that residual question.

The concern about separating chromosomal from plasmid phylogeny was addressed by an explicit final Methods description of chromosomal reconstruction and a separate plasmid phylogeny in P:S-a3b1a314f0c635f3c15c and P:S-fff7698d0ac6b7f2e097.

The concern that hypermucoidy not be reduced to capsule overproduction was addressed through revised framing. The final paper distinguishes virulence markers and notes limitations of the string test in P:S-b051b07d265d018725df.

The Figure 4 concern sought further validation or sequencing of differing plasmid bands. P:S-96b8cd68d6a960d1296a provides the final profiling figure and legend, but does not independently establish the requested additional validation.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Present the genomic contribution with its surveillance context and bounded claims.
limiting_points.text: One reviewer regarded the genomic analysis as limited in value beyond surveillance, tempering the claimed novelty of the study's broader genomic inferences.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain the carrier-genome and AMR–virulence contribution in the study framing.
supporting_points.text: The adult-carrier genomes and associated AMR–virulence observations add a distinct component to the Vietnamese hvKp genomic dataset.

questions.suggested_action: State the applicable inference boundary for comparisons between the cohorts.
questions.text: How are inferences about carriage and bloodstream infection bounded by the cohorts' different sampling periods, locations, and denominators?

questions.suggested_action: Clarify the relationship between molecular classification and clinically demonstrated hypervirulence.
questions.text: What evidence distinguishes the iucA-defined isolate category from clinical hypervirulent infection for the strains analyzed here?

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the integrated epidemiology, WGS, and plasmid-analysis description.
strengths.text: The work supplies a detailed genomic overview of Vietnamese hvKp across prevalence, population structure, virulence, AMR, and plasmid features.

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the carrier-isolate analysis alongside bloodstream isolates.
strengths.text: Including healthy adult carrier isolates broadens the dataset and enables examination of AMR–virulence features across carriage and bloodstream sources.

summary.text: The study combines bloodstream and carriage collections, whole-genome and plasmid analyses, and conjugation experiments to describe Vietnamese hvKp diversity, AMR–virulence features, carriage-related phylogenetic clustering, and helper-plasmid-associated mobilization of a non-conjugative virulence plasmid. Review feedback supports the detailed genomic and adult-carrier components, while retaining limits on cohort comparability, geographic scope, and interpretation of genotype-defined hvKp.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Scope cross-cohort and country-level interpretations to the sampled settings.
weaknesses.text: The bloodstream, adult-carriage, and child-carriage collections differ in setting and sampling period, limiting direct prevalence comparisons and nationwide generalization.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Maintain explicit genotype-versus-disease qualification wherever hvKp is interpreted.
weaknesses.text: Although the manuscript explains its molecular classification, using iucA-defined isolates as hvKp still requires care because this category does not by itself demonstrate clinical hypervirulence.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The final Methods separately specify chromosomal and virulence-plasmid phylogenetic analyses.
The final text describes molecular virulence-marker detection and limitations of the string test rather than reducing hvKp identification to hypermucoidy.
The final paper provides revised profiling presentation, but the requested sequencing or additional validation cannot be confirmed from the supplied final-paper evidence.
